newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 13.

text.p: Abortion rise spurs call for sex education: Two government ministers supported the Abortion Supervisory Committee's call for more sex education as the way to reduce abortion rates -- a call labelled naive by the Catholic Church. Page 1.
Confusion over healthcare for children may end today: Health Minister Bill English is expected to end weeks of confusion and bad press over free care for under-sixes today. Page 2.
Labour's four-point lead first poll win since 1993: Labour has overtaken National to become the most popular political party, a TVNZ-Colmar Brunton poll has found. Page 2.
Fracas report due tomorrow: Parliament's privileges committee will report on Wednesday on the fracas between Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters and National MP John Banks. Page 2.

Reserve Bank bewilders markets: The dollar jumped three-quarters of a cent and interest rates ratcheted upward on Monday after the Reserve Bank flummoxed the markets with a surprise get-tough statement. Page 15.

David Jones out of Auckland's mall project: After weeks of rumours, financially troubled Australian retailer David Jones has pulled the plug on its first overseas store in Auckland, jeopardising a $360 million inner-city development. Page 15.

Kerr sounds alarm over Budget spending: Treasurer Winston Peters's first Budget would extend the present weak phase in the economy without moves to constrain government spending, Business Roundtable chief executive Roger Kerr said on Monday. Page 15.
Chamber names chief executive: Whanganui Economic Development Corporation chief executive Claire Johnstone is the new chief executive of the Wellington Chamber of Commerce. Page 15.
